title_original: ‘Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend’ tops UK-Ireland box office as new entries flood chart
excerpt_original: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’, ‘George Michael: The Faith Tour’, ‘Wild Horse Nine’ all make top five.

Bollywood action epic Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend topped the UK-Ireland box office this weekend, as new titles dominated the top five chart.

Sony’s Ramayana started with £1.7m from 364 sites, at a £4,749 average, and has £2.2m including previews. This is the biggest opening ever for an Indian film at the UK-Ireland box office, topping the £1.6m of Dhurandhar: The Revenge from earlier this year, which had £2.1m including previews. Rise Of A Legend is the first in a two-part story, with the second part, Ramayana: Part 2 , scheduled for release in October 2028.

An ancient epic about the marriage between a young prince and princess, Ramayana is the most expensive Indian film ever made with a reported $420m budget across the two parts. Rise Of A Legend will look to challenge the £4.5m lifetime of Dhurandhar to become the highest-grossing Indian film ever in the territory.

Asian films took first and second place for the first time ever at the UK-Ireland box office, with Anime Ltd’s Godzilla Minus Zero starting with £1.1m from 474 sites at a £2,396 average and £1.4m including previews. It beat the £786,000 three-day start of 2023 first film Godzilla Minus One ; that title went on to a £2.6m total, which Minus Zero will hope to pass in the coming weeks.

Black Bear comedy-drama Wicker was the only holdover to make the top five, adding £1.1m on its second weekend after the best hold in the top 15, falling just 32%. It is up to £4.3m in a strong result.

Concert film George Michael: The Faith Tour demonstrated the variety of choices in cinemas this weekend, landing in fourth place on opening with a £1m first weekend. Playing in 592 sites for Universal, it took a £1,734 average.

Martin McDonagh’s Venice Competition title Wild Horse Nine rounded out the top five, opening to just over £1m for Disney from 660 sites at a £1,551 average. It was down on the £1.6m opening of McDonagh’s previous film The Banshees Of Inisherin from October 2022, and £2.2m start of Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri from January 2018. Wild Horse Nine has £1.5m including previews.

Despite new titles entering the charts, takings for the top five fell for the second consecutive weekend, dropping 5% to just over £6m. The coming session offers a similarly eclectic range of new releases, including heist comedy How To Rob A Bank and theatrical adaptation Prima Facie for Sony, Paramount’s Scrooge story Ebeneezer and Picturehouse Entertainment’s Palme d’Or winner Fjord .

Primetime starring Robert Pattinson posted a £844,000 second weekend for A24 – a drop of 35%, that was better than the market average. It is up to £3.5m and will look to pass £5m in the next fortnight.

Ghosts: The Possession Of Button House dropped out of the top five on its third weekend in cinemas, but still posted a healthy £747,000, falling 50%. The comedy spin-off is up to a decent £7.8m and will retain hopes of crossing £10m before it leaves cinemas, for Lionsgate.

blocks.text: Clayface leads Warner Bros’ slate, with a £683,000 third weekend after a 43% drop. It is up to £6.1m, and this week will overtake the £6.1m total of fellow DC Comics adaptation Supergirl from earlier this year.
Stray Kids World Tour Run It Live Viewing , the latest Kpop sensation concert film, took £595,000 on Saturday, November 7 alone for Trafalgar Releasing.

I Play Rocky , Peter Farrelly’s story of the making of Rocky starring Sylvester Stallone, started with £566,000 for Entertainment Film Distributors. This came from 148 sites at a decent £3,824 average, with the film having £608,000 including previews.

Stopmotion animation Wildwood added £417,000 on its third weekend for Black Bear after a 36% drop. It is up to £3.6m, overtaking the totals of fellow Laika titles Kubo And The Two Strings (£3.3m) and Missing Link (a lower £3.6m), but still behind Coraline (£8.7m) and ParaNorman (£6.4m).
Source: Carla Oset
‘La Bola Negra’

La Bola Negra scored the biggest full opening ever for a Spanish-language film at the UK-Ireland box office for Altitude. It took £536,000 including previews, ahead of the £433,000 of Pedro Almodovar’s 2006 Julieta . La Bola Negra brought in £354,000 from Friday to Sunday, from 130 sites at a strong £2,723 location average. Volver ended with £2.8m as the highest-grossing Spanish-language film ever in the territory; La Bola Negra will hold hopes of passing that mark across its run.
Universal’s DreamWorks animation Forgotten Island fell 49% on its fourth weekend in cinemas, with £318,000 taking it to a £5.6m lifetime.

Street Fighter leads Paramount’s slate, with £164,000 on its fourth session, down 66%. It is up to almost £6.1m total, with almost double the £3.4m of the highest-grossing Mortal Kombat adaptation, Mortal Kombat II from earlier this year, among other videogame spinoffs.

Amazon MGM Studios’ Verity starring Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson added £86,900 on its sixth weekend, distributed by Sony. The film is up to a decent £11.9m, the second highest-grossing Colleen Hoover adaptation behind the £21.9m of 2024’s It Ends With Us .
Ken Russell’s The Devils added £72,800 on its second weekend for BFI Distribution after a drop of 67%, and is up to £507,000.
National Theatre Live’s Golden Boy starring Josh O’Connor took £72,300 at the weekend, and is up to £265,000 following its Thursday release.
Shaun The Sheep: The Beast Of Mossy Bottom leads Studiocanal’s slate on its eighth weekend in cinemas. The Aardman stopmotion animation put on £108,000, a drop of 62%, and is up to £5.9m.

blocks.text: Resident Evil put on £61,600 on its eighth weekend for Sony, after a 69% fall brought it to £14.7m total. That is more than three times the £4.8m total of the next highest-grossing Resident Evil film, 2010’s Resident Evil: Afterlife 3D .
Other Mommy added £60,700 on its fifth weekend for Universal, with the horror from UK filmmaker Rob Savage up to £5.5m after a 77% drop.
Park Circus’s Rocky re-release took £56,500 at the weekend and has £72,200 including previews, with another £4,000 needed to become the highest-grossing re-release of John G. Avildsen’s 1976 classic.
Pawel Pawlikowski’s Fatherland added £55,800 on its third weekend for Mubi, a drop of 48%. The Cannes 2026 best director winner has £748,000 in total.
Heart Of The Beast starring Brad Pitt added £42,000 on its seventh weekend for Paramount, and is up to £7.4m total.
Paramount animation Tad And The Magic Lamp put on £31,000 on its third weekend, and has £704,000 in total.
Concert film Rammstein: Live In Mexico City brought in £28,800 from Friday to Saturday, and has just shy of £80,000 since its Wednesday opening for Trafalgar Releasing.

UK independent feature Merry Christmas Aubrey Flint started with £27,600 for Signature Entertainment, from 173 sites at a £159 location average. Including previews, the film, starring John Bradley, Celia Imrie and Richard E Grant, is up to £39,500.
The seventh weekend of Georgia Oakley’s Sense And Sensibility took £22,100 for Universal, down 62% on its previous session and up to £6.7m overall.
On its 19 th weekend in cinemas, animated favourite Minions & Monsters put on £14,100 for Universal, and is up to £20.3m.
Alejandro Gonzalez Inarritu’s Digger starring Tom Cruise put on £10,000 on its sixth weekend in cinemas, and is up to £3.1m for Warner Bros.

Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey is finally reaching the end of its journey for Universal after a £9,687 17 th weekend in cinemas. The epic has £88.4m in total, as the 10 th highest-grossing film of all time.
Boots Riley’s I Love Boosters dropped 83% on its second weekend in cinemas with £5,547, and is up to £164,000 for Universal.
Screenbound Pictures opened Western Dead Souls to £4,777 from two sites, with £6,350 including previews and final results still to come.
Central City Media’s re-release of Zhang Yimou’s Venice Silver Lion winner Raise The Red Lantern brought in £4,457, with the film having made £93,700 on its original 1992 release.
Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning put on £4,339 on its fifth weekend for Sony and is up to £1.7m, down on the £10.7m of 2010 predecessor The Social Network .
Ashley Walters’ debut feature Animol added £1,099 on its second weekend for Studiocanal, and is up to £83,600.
A V For Vendetta re-release brought in £937 at the weekend for Park Circus, with £16,700 in total since its Thursday opening.

Summer blockbuster Spider-Man: Brand New Day added £383 on its 15 th weekend in cinemas, and has £100.2m across its lifetime for Sony, as the third-highest-grossing film of all time behind Star Wars: The Force Awakens (£123.3m) and Skyfall (£102.8m).
Sony anime The Irregular At Magic High School – Yoruba Succession Arc took £92 at the weekend, with £3,127 since its opening on Wednesday, November 4.
UK independent drama Amazing Grace posted a £4,281 opening for Screenbound Pictures, with final Friday-to-Sunday figures still to come.
